```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r readModelDb("Wen_2026_salbutamol_pbpk")()$reference`
* Description: `r readModelDb("Wen_2026_salbutamol_pbpk")()$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40262-026-01664-y> (open access; PMC13461897)
* Supplement: electronic supplementary material 1 of the article (Table S1
  lung physiology and the NONMEM control stream of the lung model)

Wen et al. built a population minimal PBPK model of orally inhaled salbutamol
from one clinical study in which every volunteer was sampled with three lung
techniques: bronchosorption (bronchial epithelial lining fluid, ELF), bronchial
mucosal biopsy, and bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL, ELF averaged over the whole
lung), alongside plasma. The model was then used for stochastic
simulation-estimation of lung sampling designs. Only the fitted PK model is
packaged here; the simulation-estimation study (Figures 3 and 6) re-estimates
the model on simulated data and has no further model to extract.

The same authors' earlier rat model of salbutamol, on which the lung
structure of this model is based, is available as
`Wen_2025_salbutamol_rat_pbpk`.

# Population

Thirteen healthy, non-smoking adults aged 18-50 years with normal lung function
(inhalation cohort of ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03524066) each inhaled a single
200 ug dose of commercial salbutamol through a spacer. Each had two bronchoscopy
sessions (1 and 6 h, 2 and 9 h, 3 and 12 h, or 4 and 18 h after the dose), with
two bronchosorption samples, one BAL and two biopsies per session, and plasma
samples at 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12 and 24 h. In total 101 plasma and 100 lung
samples (32 bronchosorption, 32 biopsy, 36 BAL) were analysed. Wen 2026 does not
restate weight or sex distribution; the model has no covariates.

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Wen_2026_salbutamol_pbpk")()$population)
```

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `lcl` (CL) | 32.8 L/h | Table 3 |
| `lvc` (V) | 211 L | Table 3 |
| `lka_oral` (ka) | 2.01 1/h | Table 3 |
| `lkdiss` (kdiss) | 1000 1/h, fixed | Table 3; Methods (Eq 2 text) |
| `logitfdepot_lung` (F1) | logit(0.5) = 0, fixed | Table 3 |
| `lfdepot_oral` (F2) | 0.418, fixed | Table 3 |
| `fdep_bronchial`, `fdep_bronchiolar` | 0.0992, 0.226 (alveolar = remainder), fixed | NONMEM code `FBB`, `FBR` (supplement); Results text 9.90 / 22.6 / 67.5 % |
| `lbp`, `lfuelf`, `lfu` | 0.96, 0.74, 0.65, fixed | Table 3 |
| `lkpulung` (Kp,u,lung) | 11.0 | Table 3 |
| `lpeff` (Peff) | 0.543 | Table 3 |
| `etalcl` | 0.193^2 | Table 3, 'CV% Clearance' 19.3 |
| `etalogitfdepot_lung` | 1.285^2 | Table 3, 'CV% LogitF1' 128.5 |
| `expSd`, `expSd_Cbr`, `expSd_Cbr_tissue`, `expSd_Celf` | 0.188, 1.09, 0.848, 1.46 | Table 3 (plasma, bronchosorption, biopsy, BAL) |
| ELF / epithelium / interstitium volumes and ELF surface areas | per region | Table S1 and NONMEM code |
| Epithelium surface areas | 317.61, 2896.77, 700000 cm2 | NONMEM code (`SBB_EPI`, `SBar_EPI`, `SAV_EPI`) |
| Regional blood flows | 1.05, 8.07, 312 L/h | Table S1 and NONMEM code (`QBB`, `Qbar`, `QAV = 5.2 L/min`) |
| `d/dt(elf_*)` | Eq 2 | Methods; NONMEM code `DADT(5)`, `DADT(8)`, `DADT(11)` |
| `d/dt(epi_*)` | Eq 3 | Methods; NONMEM code `DADT(6)`, `DADT(9)`, `DADT(12)` |
| `d/dt(sub_*)` | Eqs 4-5 | Methods; NONMEM code `DADT(7)`, `DADT(10)`, `DADT(13)` |
| `d/dt(central)` | one-compartment, oral + three lung inputs | Methods; NONMEM code `DADT(14)` |
| Dose split `f()` | `F1 x f_region` to each lung depot, `F2 x (1 - F1)` to the gut | Eq 1; NONMEM code `F1`-`F4` |
| `Cbr`, `Cbr_tissue`, `Celf` | bronchial ELF; bronchial ELF + epithelium + interstitium; mean ELF of all regions | Methods (Population-Based PBPK Modelling, last paragraph); NONMEM `$ERROR` |
| Residual model | additive on log-transformed data | Methods (Data Description and Data Handling); NONMEM `$ERROR` |

# Dosing

The model has four dosing compartments, one per deposition site, exactly as
the authors' data set. One inhalation of `dose` ug is therefore four dose
records of `dose` ug each; each depot keeps its own fraction through `f()`.

```{r events}
mod <- readModelDb("Wen_2026_salbutamol_pbpk")
ui <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)

dose_cmts <- c(
  "depot_lung_bronchial", "depot_lung_bronchiolar",
  "depot_lung_alveolar", "depot_oral"
)

make_events <- function(n, obs_times, dose = 200, id_offset = 0L) {
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n)
  doses <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, cmt = dose_cmts) |>
    dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = dose, evid = 1L, dvid = NA_integer_)
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(cmt = "central", amt = 0, evid = 0L, dvid = 1L)
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
    as.data.frame()
}
```

Observation rows sit on the `central` state with `dvid = 1`; the model declares
four endpoints, and the solve returns every endpoint column (`Cc`, `Cbr`,
`Cbr_tissue`, `Celf`) on every row.

# Typical-subject profiles

```{r typical}
obs_grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.05), seq(2.25, 24, by = 0.25))))
ev_typ <- make_events(1, obs_grid)
typ <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ui), ev_typ))

typ |>
  dplyr::select(time, Cc, Cbr, Cbr_tissue, Celf) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "output", values_to = "conc") |>
  dplyr::filter(time > 0) |>
  dplyr::mutate(output = factor(
    output,
    levels = c("Cbr", "Cbr_tissue", "Celf", "Cc"),
    labels = c("Bronchosorption", "Biopsy", "BAL (ELF)", "Plasma")
  )) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, conc)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~output, nrow = 1) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Salbutamol (ug/L)",
    title = "Typical subject, 200 ug inhaled"
  )
```

# Replicate Figure 2: visual predictive check

Figure 2 of Wen 2026 shows the observations with the model-predicted median
(lung panels) and 5th / 50th / 95th percentiles (plasma). The simulation below
uses 200 virtual subjects and adds each technique's residual error on the log
scale, as a VPC does.

```{r figure-2}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20260110)
set.seed(20260110)

vpc_times <- c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 12, 18, 24)
ev_vpc <- make_events(200, vpc_times)
sim_vpc <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(ui, ev_vpc))

theta <- setNames(ui$iniDf$est, ui$iniDf$name)
add_ruv <- function(x, sd) x * exp(stats::rnorm(length(x), 0, sd))

vpc_long <- sim_vpc |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Bronchosorption = add_ruv(Cbr, theta[["expSd_Cbr"]]),
    Biopsy = add_ruv(Cbr_tissue, theta[["expSd_Cbr_tissue"]]),
    BAL = add_ruv(Celf, theta[["expSd_Celf"]]),
    Plasma = add_ruv(Cc, theta[["expSd"]])
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Bronchosorption, Biopsy, BAL, Plasma) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(id, time), names_to = "technique", values_to = "conc") |>
  dplyr::mutate(technique = factor(
    technique,
    levels = c("Bronchosorption", "Biopsy", "BAL", "Plasma")
  ))

vpc_long |>
  dplyr::group_by(technique, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q05 = stats::quantile(conc, 0.05),
    Q50 = stats::median(conc),
    Q95 = stats::quantile(conc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25, fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_line(linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~technique, nrow = 1) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.01, 1000)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Salbutamol (ug/L)",
    title = "Simulated 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles",
    caption = "Replicates the prediction intervals of Figure 2 of Wen 2026."
  )
```

The simulated medians follow the dashed medians of Figure 2: bronchosorption
falls from a few hundred ug/L at 1 h to about 0.07 ug/L at 18 h, biopsy from
about 40 to 2 ug/L between 1 and 9 h, and plasma peaks near 0.5 ug/L and falls
to a few hundredths of a ug/L at 24 h.

# Replicate Figures 4 and 5: drugs of different permeability

Wen 2026 simulated hypothetical compounds with `Peff` 10-fold higher, 10-fold
lower and 100-fold lower than salbutamol, keeping every other parameter at its
final estimate and including the residual errors. Figure 4 shows the three lung
matrices and Figure 5 the ratio of the BAL-derived ELF concentration to the
plasma concentration. The paper used 1000 subjects per scenario; 200 are used
here.

```{r permeability-sim}
peff_scen <- tibble::tibble(
  scenario = c("High permeability", "Salbutamol", "Low permeability", "Very low permeability"),
  peff_mult = c(10, 1, 0.1, 0.01)
)
ep_times <- c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 24)
fig4_times <- sort(unique(c(ep_times, seq(0.5, 24, by = 0.5))))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20260111)
set.seed(20260111)
sim_perm <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(peff_scen)), function(i) {
  ui_i <- rxode2::ini(ui, lpeff = log(0.543 * peff_scen$peff_mult[i]))
  out <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(ui_i, make_events(200, fig4_times)))
  out$scenario <- peff_scen$scenario[i]
  out
})) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    scenario = factor(scenario, levels = peff_scen$scenario),
    Bronchosorption = add_ruv(Cbr, theta[["expSd_Cbr"]]),
    Biopsy = add_ruv(Cbr_tissue, theta[["expSd_Cbr_tissue"]]),
    BAL = add_ruv(Celf, theta[["expSd_Celf"]]),
    Plasma = add_ruv(Cc, theta[["expSd"]]),
    ep_ratio = BAL / Plasma
  )
```

```{r figure-4, fig.height = 7}
sim_perm |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, scenario, Bronchosorption, Biopsy, BAL) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Bronchosorption, Biopsy, BAL), names_to = "technique", values_to = "conc") |>
  dplyr::mutate(technique = factor(technique, levels = c("Bronchosorption", "Biopsy", "BAL"))) |>
  dplyr::group_by(scenario, technique, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q25 = stats::quantile(conc, 0.25),
    Q50 = stats::median(conc),
    Q75 = stats::quantile(conc, 0.75),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_line(colour = "red3") +
  geom_line(aes(y = Q25), colour = "red3", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(aes(y = Q75), colour = "red3", linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_grid(scenario ~ technique) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Drug concentration (ug/L)",
    caption = "Replicates the median and interquartile range of Figure 4 of Wen 2026."
  )
```

```{r figure-5}
ep_sum <- sim_perm |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% ep_times) |>
  dplyr::group_by(scenario, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q25 = stats::quantile(ep_ratio, 0.25),
    Q50 = stats::median(ep_ratio),
    Q75 = stats::quantile(ep_ratio, 0.75),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Population medians of the ELF-to-plasma ratio read by eye by the maintainers
# from the solid red lines of Figure 5 (log axis, so each value is good to
# roughly a factor of 1.5).
fig5 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario, ~time, ~published,
  "High permeability", 0.25, 30,
  "High permeability", 1, 1.2,
  "High permeability", 4, 1.0,
  "High permeability", 8, 0.95,
  "High permeability", 12, 1.0,
  "High permeability", 24, 0.95,
  "Salbutamol", 0.25, 500,
  "Salbutamol", 1, 80,
  "Salbutamol", 2, 30,
  "Salbutamol", 4, 7,
  "Salbutamol", 8, 1.4,
  "Salbutamol", 12, 1.05,
  "Salbutamol", 24, 1.0,
  "Low permeability", 0.25, 7000,
  "Low permeability", 1, 800,
  "Low permeability", 2, 650,
  "Low permeability", 4, 420,
  "Low permeability", 8, 270,
  "Low permeability", 12, 290,
  "Low permeability", 24, 330,
  "Very low permeability", 0.25, 23000,
  "Very low permeability", 1, 11000,
  "Very low permeability", 2, 9500,
  "Very low permeability", 4, 4500,
  "Very low permeability", 8, 2700,
  "Very low permeability", 12, 3500,
  "Very low permeability", 24, 8000
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(scenario = factor(scenario, levels = peff_scen$scenario))

ggplot(ep_sum, aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_line(colour = "red3") +
  geom_line(aes(y = Q25), colour = "red3", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(aes(y = Q75), colour = "red3", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(data = fig5, aes(y = published), shape = 4, size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(~scenario, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "BAL-derived ELF-to-plasma ratio",
    caption = paste(
      "Lines: simulated median and interquartile range.",
      "Crosses: medians read from Figure 5 of Wen 2026."
    )
  )

ep_cmp <- dplyr::inner_join(ep_sum, fig5, by = c("scenario", "time")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(fold = Q50 / published)

ep_cmp |>
  dplyr::group_by(scenario) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    `Median fold (simulated / Figure 5)` = signif(stats::median(fold), 3),
    `Smallest fold` = signif(min(fold), 3),
    `Largest fold` = signif(max(fold), 3),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(Scenario = scenario) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated vs. Figure 5 median ELF-to-plasma ratios.")
```

The ratio is a demanding check of the lung structure, because it spans four
orders of magnitude across the permeability scenarios and depends on `Peff`,
`Kp,u,lung`, the unbound fractions and the regional volumes and surface areas
all at once. A mis-scaled permeability (for example a factor-1000 error in the
area or permeability units) would shift whole curves by orders of magnitude.

```{r figure-5-check}
stopifnot(
  # Centre of each scenario's curve within a factor of 2 of the published one.
  all(abs(log(tapply(ep_cmp$fold, ep_cmp$scenario, stats::median))) < log(2)),
  # Salbutamol's ratio settles near 1 after 8 h, as stated in the Results.
  all(abs(log(ep_sum$Q50[ep_sum$scenario == "Salbutamol" & ep_sum$time >= 12])) < log(1.5))
)
```

# PKNCA validation

Wen 2026 reports no NCA. Because no drug is eliminated from the lung, every
deposited microgram eventually reaches plasma, so the plasma AUC from zero to
infinity has a closed form for each subject:
`AUC = dose x (F1 + F2 x (1 - F1)) / CL`. PKNCA on the simulated plasma
profiles is compared against that closed form, subject by subject and at the
typical-value level.

```{r pknca}
nca_times <- sort(unique(c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 24, 36, 48, 72)))
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20260112)
sim_nca_raw <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(ui, make_events(200, nca_times)))
sim_nca_raw$treatment <- "200 ug inhaled"

sim_nca <- sim_nca_raw |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
sim_nca <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> dplyr::distinct(id, treatment) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, treatment, time)

dose_df <- sim_nca |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = 200)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

indiv <- sim_nca_raw |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, cl, fdepot_lung) |>
  dplyr::mutate(auc_closed = 200 * (fdepot_lung + 0.418 * (1 - fdepot_lung)) / cl)
auc_chk <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  dplyr::select(id, aucinf = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(indiv, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (aucinf / auc_closed - 1))

summary(auc_chk$pct_diff)
```

```{r pknca-check}
# Same drawn parameters on both sides, so the difference is trapezoidal and
# extrapolation error only.
stopifnot(
  abs(stats::median(auc_chk$pct_diff)) < 2,
  stats::quantile(abs(auc_chk$pct_diff), 0.9) < 5
)
```

## Comparison against typical values

The reference values are the typical subject's closed-form plasma AUC
(`200 x (0.5 + 0.418 x 0.5) / 32.8`) and the one-compartment elimination
half-life (`log(2) x 211 / 32.8`); Wen 2026 itself tabulates neither.

```{r nca-compare}
typical_ref <- data.frame(
  treatment = "200 ug inhaled",
  aucinf.obs = 200 * (0.5 + 0.418 * 0.5) / 32.8,
  half.life = log(2) * 211 / 32.8
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = typical_ref,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(aucinf.obs = "ug*h/L", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Simulated (median of 200 subjects) vs. typical-value closed forms. * differs by >20%."
)
```

The simulated median AUC sits close to the typical value because the
inter-individual variability on the logit lung fraction is nearly symmetric
around F1 = 0.5. The terminal half-life is that of plasma elimination: drug
leaves the lung much faster than it is cleared from plasma.

# Dissolution rate: paper versus supplement code

Table 3 and the Methods fix `kdiss` at 1000 1/h; the NONMEM control stream in
the supplement fixes the corresponding constant (`KA2`) at 31.6 1/h, the lung
absorption rate of the earlier salbutamol meta-analysis model
(`Courlet_2022_salbutamol_mbma`). The packaged model follows Table 3. Both
values make dissolution complete within minutes, so the choice barely matters
at the sampled times:

```{r kdiss}
typ_slow <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(rxode2::ini(ui, lkdiss = log(31.6))),
  ev_typ
))
kdiss_diff <- data.frame(
  time = typ$time,
  Cbr = 100 * (typ_slow$Cbr / typ$Cbr - 1),
  Cc = 100 * (typ_slow$Cc / typ$Cc - 1)
) |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= 0.5)
signif(sapply(kdiss_diff[, c("Cbr", "Cc")], function(x) max(abs(x))), 3)
stopifnot(max(abs(kdiss_diff$Cbr)) < 5, max(abs(kdiss_diff$Cc)) < 5)
```

The largest difference from 0.5 h onwards is a few percent, against residual
errors of 19-146 % on the log scale.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Two-step fit packaged as one model.** The authors estimated the systemic
  parameters from plasma alone, then fixed them and supplied each subject's
  post hoc `CL` and lung fraction `F1` as data to the lung step (the supplement
  code reads `CL` and `Fr` from `$INPUT`). The packaged model carries the
  first step's inter-individual variability on `CL` and logit `F1` instead, so
  that it simulates new subjects.
- **IIV scale.** Table 3 reports both random effects as 'CV%', but a CV is
  undefined for an eta on the logit scale, so the column is read as
  100 x sqrt(omega^2) and the variances are 0.193^2 and 1.285^2. The plasma
  residual SD reads the same way: the supplement's initial `$SIGMA` of 0.0352
  for plasma is 18.8 % as a square root, matching Table 3.
- **Residual error.** Concentrations were log-transformed and fitted with an
  additive error, encoded as `lnorm()` with Table 3's percentages as SDs on
  the log scale. The vignette's stochastic figures add this error by hand
  because the four endpoints share one observation row.
- **Differences between the paper and the authors' published code.**
  - Table S1 prints the epithelium surface areas as 1.74, 4.25 and
    3.58 cm2, the same numbers as the epithelium volumes in mL two rows
    above. The NONMEM code uses 317.61, 2896.77 and 700000 cm2; the code's
    values are used.
  - `kdiss` is 1000 1/h in Table 3 and 31.6 1/h in the code; Table 3 is used
    (see the section above, which shows the difference is negligible).
  - The code's `$THETA` records hold initial estimates (`Kp,u,lung` 11.16,
    `Peff` 0.563, V 212 L, oral ka 2.03 1/h, the last two fixed from an
    earlier run). The final estimates of Table 3 are used.
  - The code sets the bronchial deposition fraction to 0.0992, which the
    Results round to 9.90 %; the code's value is used. The alveolar fraction is
    the remainder, 0.6748 (67.5 % in the text).
- **Permeability units.** In the code each diffusion flux is
  `Peff x area x concentration` with the area in m2, the volume in L and no
  further unit factor, so the fitted `Peff` is numerically in L/h per m2
  (10^-3 m/h), although Table 3 labels it m/h. The model follows the code's
  arithmetic, which is what the estimate belongs to; the reproduction of the
  four permeability scenarios of Figure 5 above depends on it. In those units
  the estimate corresponds to 5.4 x 10^-4 m/h, close to the 4.2 x 10^-4 m/h
  the same authors estimated in rats (Wen 2025), rather than 1000-fold higher
  as the Discussion states.
- **Spacer loss** was not modelled by the authors; the nominal 200 ug dose
  enters the four depots.
- **Figure 5 medians** were read by eye by the maintainers from the published
  figure and are good to about a factor of 1.5 on its log axis.
- No erratum or correction notice was found for Wen 2026 on Europe PMC as of
  2026-11-16.
